page: OVHcloud b3-512 is a General Purpose cloud server instance powered by an x86_64 architecture with 128 dedicated physical cores from the AMD EPYC family running at 2.3 GHz. Configured with a single thread per core and no hyperthreading, the instance provides 512 GB of system RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation of 4.0 GB per core. Local storage is provisioned via a 400 GB NVMe SSD, and baseline network throughput is rated at 20 Gbps. The server operates without discrete GPU hardware acceleration.

Benchmark results demonstrate top-tier multi-core computing capability, with the instance placing in the top decile for PassMark CPU (113,810.76), Geekbench multi-core (20,790.0), and multi-core stress-ng tests. In-memory and caching metrics are similarly strong, highlighted by Redis SET throughput reaching 169.74 million operations per second and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression achieving 1,158.47 GB/sec. Conversely, single-threaded operations perform in the average range, including a Geekbench single-core score of 1,891.0, reflecting standard clock speed constraints.

The 128 dedicated physical cores provide resource efficiency for highly parallelized workloads without the overhead of thread contention. However, local storage capacity is limited to 400 GB, requiring external storage configurations for large-scale persistence. Additionally, the lack of hardware accelerators makes it unsuited for intensive autoregressive large language model generation. The server is primarily suitable for large-scale code compilation, high-concurrency microservices, in-memory Redis caches, and batch data processing.
description: OVHcloud b3-512 is a general-purpose cloud instance provisioned with 128 dedicated AMD EPYC physical cores running at 2.3 GHz, 512 GB of RAM, 400 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, and 20 Gbps network bandwidth. Engineered for high parallelism, the instance achieves top-decile multi-threaded performance in stress-ng, Geekbench, and PassMark tests, complementing a high-capacity memory architecture that drives over 169 million Redis SET operations per second. The balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio provides solid resource distribution for compute-dense tasks without memory bloat. Single-threaded execution remains average, reflecting standard core clock limits, and the lack of discrete GPUs limits heavy generative AI tasks. The instance is suitable for high-concurrency software builds, parallel data transformations, high-throughput in-memory caching, distributed microservices, and general compute workloads requiring dedicated core performance.
